title: Skill Description Trigger Tester
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI for EE Research
description: Trigger-test activity in which learners read one illustrative skill description for checking SPICE netlists and decide, for eight user requests in a fixed order, whether an agent should load the skill. Each request gets one attempt, followed by Correct or the correct answer with a one-sentence reason. The run ends with a score out of 8, a mastery statement at 7 of 8, and the list of near-miss requests that share a keyword with the description but should not trigger.

educational.topic: Testing whether an agent skill description triggers on the right requests
learningObjectives: Distinguish, for each of eight user requests, whether a stated skill description should trigger the skill or not, with at least 7 of 8 correct
Separate the task a request asks for from the vocabulary it shares with a skill description

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description; all controls are native HTML buttons reachable with the Tab key and expose aria-pressed for the selected answer; correct and incorrect feedback uses a color-blind-safe blue and vermillion pair together with check-mark and X symbols and words; text is 16 px, reduced to no less than 14 px only at narrow widths.

controls.label: Should trigger
controls.purpose: Selects the answer Should trigger for the current request. Disabled after the answer is submitted.

controls.label: Should not trigger
controls.purpose: Selects the answer Should not trigger for the current request. Disabled after the answer is submitted.

controls.label: Submit / Next Request / See Score
controls.purpose: Submit commits the selected answer (one attempt per request). After submission the button advances to the next request, and after request 8 it shows the score.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Binary judgment on near-miss and covered requests with immediate explanatory feedback
keyQuestions: Would an agent load this skill for this request?
Does the request ask for the task the description names?
Does the request name an input type the description covers?
commonMisconceptions: Any request that shares a keyword with the description should trigger the skill
A request that is about the same files but for a different task should trigger it
A skill should trigger on any request that mentions its domain
assessmentOpportunities: At least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt is evidence of mastery
Learner names the shared keyword and the actual task of each near-miss request on the summary screen
